tool_args.old_string:
\paragraph{Synthesis.}
VLA fine-tuning produces two training-induced representational changes---$R^2$ exit collapse and counterfactual sensitivity---that concentrate at the readout token (training shifts readout $R^2$ by $+0.069$ vs.\ image\_mean by $+0.015$).
L1 instruction attention is inherited from base-model pretraining (Phi-3-Vision: 32/32, Qwen2.5-VL: 13--14/16 before training).
VLA fine-tuning does not build instruction routing from scratch; downstream representations differ between trained and untrained models while early-layer attention structure is preserved.

\paragraph{Cross-architecture consistency.}
Two independent VLM-to-VLA transitions converge on the same training-induced effects (observed in all 6 cells), compatible with task-structure constraints of causal-decoder VLA design.
OpenVLA provides supplementary VLA-to-VLA evidence, with exit collapse observed in 2/4 cells for spatially demanding tasks; however, the OXE pretraining confound limits direct comparison with VLM-to-VLA transitions.
Mid-layer probes outperform exit-layer probes for action prediction in architectures exhibiting exit collapse, suggesting potential efficiency gains from early-exit inference.
Correlating trained $\Delta R^2$ with LIBERO success rates yields a positive but non-significant trend ($\rho = 0.583$, $p = 0.10$, $n = 9$; Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_discussion_appendix}).

\paragraph{Synthesis.}
VLA fine-tuning produces two training-induced representational changes---$R^2$ exit collapse and counterfactual sensitivity---that concentrate at the readout token (training shifts readout $R^2$ by $+0.069$ vs.\ image\_mean by $+0.015$).
L1 instruction attention is inherited from base-model pretraining (Phi-3-Vision: 32/32, Qwen2.5-VL: 13--14/16 before training).
VLA fine-tuning does not build instruction routing from scratch; downstream representations differ between trained and untrained models while early-layer attention structure is preserved.

\paragraph{VLM-to-VLA vs.\ VLA-to-VLA transitions.}
Demo-level clustered bootstrap reveals a clean separation: significant exit collapse in all VLM-to-VLA trained cells (95\% CI excludes zero) but in none of the VLA-to-VLA cells (0/4 OpenVLA suites reach significance).
Two independent VLM-to-VLA transitions (TracVLA and NORA, with distinct backbone families) converge on the same effect, compatible with task-structure constraints of causal-decoder VLA design rather than architecture-specific artifacts.
The absence of significant collapse under VLA-to-VLA conditions is consistent with the OXE-pretrained baseline having already undergone exit-layer reorganization during its initial action training on 970K episodes; LIBERO fine-tuning, operating on a model that has already adapted for action prediction, does not produce further exit collapse.
Mid-layer probes outperform exit-layer probes for action prediction in architectures exhibiting significant collapse, suggesting potential efficiency gains from early-exit inference.
Correlating trained $\Delta R^2$ with LIBERO success rates yields a positive but non-significant trend ($\rho = 0.583$, $p = 0.10$, $n = 9$; Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_discussion_appendix}).

\paragraph{Conclusion.}
We analyzed three VLA architectures across four LIBERO task suites, comparing trained and untrained checkpoints.
Two training-induced effects---$R^2$ exit collapse (observed in all 6 VLM-to-VLA cells) and counterfactual sensitivity ($d = 0.45$--$1.52$)---differ consistently between trained and untrained conditions across architectures, while L1 instruction attention is inherited from base-model priors.
An NLP finetuning control ($\Delta R^2 = 0.000$) is consistent with exit collapse being specific to action-oriented training.
Code and data will be released upon acceptance.

1	We analyze how VLA fine-tuning reorganizes instruction routing by comparing three architectures---OpenVLA (Llama-2-7B), TracVLA (Phi-3-mini), and NORA (Qwen2.5-VL-3B)---across four LIBERO task suites in trained and untrained conditions ($N = 2$ independent VLM-to-VLA transitions, plus one VLA-to-VLA transition).

\paragraph{NLP finetuning control.}
To test whether exit collapse is specific to action-oriented training or a generic fine-tuning artifact, we probe Llama-2-7b-chat---the same Llama-2-7B backbone as OpenVLA, fine-tuned via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) for conversational use, without an action head or any robot demonstration data.
This control isolates the effect of action-oriented training: the backbone architecture, model scale (7B parameters), and fine-tuning regime (instruction tuning on the base Llama-2-7B) are matched, while the training objective (chat vs.\ action prediction) differs.
Across all 32 layers, the $R^2$ action-probe profile is completely flat ($R^2 = 0.155 \pm 0.001$, $\Delta R^2 = 0.000$), showing no peak-to-exit drop.
By comparison, VLM-to-VLA trained models exhibit pronounced collapse ($\Delta R^2 = 0.156$--$0.362$); OpenVLA (same backbone, VLA-to-VLA) shows $\Delta R^2 = 0.034$--$0.116$.
The absence of any exit collapse in the chat-finetuned control rules out the explanation that exit collapse is a generic consequence of fine-tuning a language model.
